                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying neuronal regeneration. For microscopic visualization of the neuron, an aniline stain is applied. After staining, only the soma and dendrites of the neurons are visualized, not the axon. Presence of which of the following cellular elements best explains this staining pattern?

                    ### Options

opb. Nucleus
opc. Lysosome
opd. Golgi apparatus
ope. Rough endoplasmic reticulum

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The staining pattern showing only the soma and dendrites of neurons after aniline staining can be best explained by the presence of the Golgi apparatus. The Golgi apparatus is involved in packaging and transporting proteins within the cell, including post-translational modifications. It is also involved in the synthesis of lysosomes, which contain enzymes that digest cellular waste. This staining pattern aligns with the Golgi apparatus's role in protein processing and lysosome synthesis.
